history.summary:
Basketball was invented in December 1891 by Canadian-American physical education instructor Dr. James Naismith in Springfield, Massachusetts, using peach baskets and a soccer ball. Originally designed as an indoor winter conditioning activity, the game rapidly spread across U.S. colleges and international YMCAs, becoming an official Olympic medal sport at the 1936 Berlin Games.

Following the merger of the BAA and NBL to form the National Basketball Association (NBA) in 1949, basketball evolved into a global cultural and athletic powerhouse. By 2026, the sport features unprecedented international parity, high-pace three-point analytics, global superstars dominating leagues across North America and Europe, and record-breaking growth in women's professional and international competition.

key_eras.description: Creation of Naismith's 13 original rules, rise of NCAA tournament basketball, and debut at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.
Introduction of the 24-second shot clock, Bill Russell's 11 championships with Boston, and Wilt Chamberlain's statistical dominance.
Global television explosion sparked by Magic Johnson and Larry Bird, Michael Jordan's six titles, and the 1992 Barcelona Olympic Dream Team.
The three-point revolution led by Stephen Curry, LeBron James' longevity records, and international superstars like Jokić, Antetokounmpo, and Wembanyama.
